clue.text: Centre of inferior quality

definitions.meaning: a headquarters or hub of operations, as in a military camp
low, poor or debased, as in a cheap metal

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: a headquarters or hub, and the adjective for low-grade or debased material.

clue.text: Making mistake chopping head off fish

indicators.note: cutting off the head means removing the opening letter of the fish

parts.note: the herring is a common silvery sea fish

explanation.surface: Someone blunders while beheading a fish for the pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Straying from what is right is going wrong, the participle sense of committing an error.

clue.text: Insect landing on fine meat

indicators.note: in a down answer, the insect settles on top of the following letter

parts.note: a bee is a flying insect
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A bee alights on a choice cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat from cattle; the general word is defined by its broader category.

clue.text: Fighting court case

definitions.meaning: a lawsuit brought before a judge

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: combat in war, and legal proceedings brought against someone.

clue.text: Area DI observing rules very closely

parts.note: taken as written; DI is the abbreviation for a Detective Inspector
rigid, rule-bound, exacting

explanation.surface: A police detective inspector sticks rigidly to procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: A region or locality marked out for administration is a synonym for an area.

clue.text: Promises no changes — an error in speech

indicators.note: the letters of the first two words are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A politician's broken promises are dismissed as a mere slip of the tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is fair because the slip, named after the Reverend Spooner, swaps the initial sounds of words, as 'tons of soil' for 'sons of toil'.
explanation.definitionFit: A verbal slip transposing the opening sounds of words, named after an Oxford don.

clue.text: A centre in the Parisian ball game

indicators.note: the article phrase goes inside the French word for 'the'

parts.note: le is French for 'the'
in football a centre is a cross, a ball played into the middle

explanation.surface: A footballer plays a cross in a Paris match.
explanation.definitionFit: A team sport played with a ball and netted sticks, originally North American.

clue.text: Bird in spring on river bank

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
R is the map abbreviation for river
a bank is a row, as a bank of seats or switches

explanation.surface: A little bird perches by a spring on the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brown songbird, a familiar example of the class.

clue.text: Closer game? Lose out, but well done!

indicators.note: these letters are taken out of the first word of the clue

parts.note: I spy is a children's guessing game

explanation.surface: A tight contest, a loser out, and a cry of congratulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lose out' removes LOSE from CLOSER to leave CR. 'Well done!' looks like praise but means cooked thoroughly.
explanation.definitionFit: Food cooked thoroughly until brittle on the outside, as in thoroughly cooked bacon.

clue.text: Remarkable reign associated with a queen

indicators.note: read as re-markable: the letters of the next word can be marked out again in new order

explanation.surface: A long and memorable reign belongs to a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for queen, used in the title of a reigning female monarch.

clue.text: Tall tale about king causes disagreement

indicators.note: the made-up story goes around the royal letter

parts.note: an untrue story is fiction
R, from Rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A boastful story about a monarch stirs up discord.
explanation.definitionFit: Conflict or rubbing between people, the figurative sense of resistance between surfaces.

clue.text: Very imposing — that's how actors are on the cinema screen

definitions.meaning: flamboyant, exaggerated, larger in personality than ordinary people

definitions.text: that's how actors are on the cinema screen
definitions.meaning: projected far bigger than their real size on a big screen

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for an outsized personality, and literally how film images exceed real-life scale.

clue.text: Also short of bubbly, etc

parts.note: and means also, in addition

indicators.note: something bubbly is effervescent and agitated, so the letters fizz into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone lists what is lacking: no champagne, and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bubbly' looks like champagne but shuffles the letters of 'short of' into SOFORTH.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation etc, et cetera, means the rest of a list continues likewise.

clue.text: Hitch up in Hawick, they say

indicators.note: signals the town's name as spoken by people

parts.note: a Scottish Borders town, pronounced locally like 'hoik'

explanation.surface: Someone tugs up their trousers in a Scottish Borders town.
explanation.walkthrough: Hawick is a town in the Scottish Borders whose name is said with one syllable.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British word for yanking or lifting something abruptly, like trousers.

clue.text: Not even second chances

parts.note: a number that is not even is odd

explanation.surface: No further opportunity, not even a second try.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting ratios or likelihoods are synonyms for probabilities or chances.

clue.text: Reconstructed Swedish boxing ring is minor attraction

indicators.note: the rearranged letters enclose the round letter
rebuilt, so the letters of the nationality are put together in another order

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A rebuilt Swedish boxing ring becomes a little fairground draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' puts O inside SIDESHW, the anagram of SWEDISH from 'Reconstructed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small subsidiary show at a fair or circus, secondary to the main event.

clue.text: Strange, the two of us following one road? On the contrary

indicators.note: with 'On the contrary', the pronoun comes first and the numeral and road follow it

parts.note: we means the speaker and one other
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Odd that we two should follow the same road.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally the pronoun would come after the numeral and road; 'On the contrary' reverses that order.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd, uncanny or bizarre are all straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Current doctor caught head of clinic out

indicators.note: the chosen letter is taken out of the word before it
takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A physician has been taken ill with a chill caught outside the clinic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of clinic' gives C, and 'out' removes it from CAUGHT to leave AUGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A current of air, as through a gap under a door, is a draught.

clue.text: Dog story heard

indicators.note: a word that is heard is spoken, so the sound matters

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A story about a dog, overheard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' is a verb here, meaning follow closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To shadow or follow someone closely is to dog them.

clue.text: Pensioners initially sang in tune in minstrel style

definitions.meaning: elderly people living in a care home or with family

definitions.text: initially sang in tune in minstrel style
definitions.meaning: a Stephen Foster song first performed by Christy's Minstrels

explanation.definitionFit: Elderly people at home, and the title of the Foster song also called Swanee River.

clue.text: Senior citizens love stories about duke

parts.note: O is love, a zero score in tennis

indicators.note: the untruths go around the noble's letter

parts.note: lies are untrue stories

explanation.surface: Elderly people relish gossip about a duke.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal word for elderly people, also used for old songs or films.

clue.text: Husband and his mother's sisters must be locals?

parts.note: a parent's sisters are a person's aunts

explanation.surface: A husband's maternal relations must be neighbours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locals' here is a noun, the places people frequent, such as a pub called one's local.
explanation.definitionFit: Favourite places frequently visited, such as one's regular pub, are hangouts.

clue.text: Deliberate trick by team on right

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A deliberate deception by a team playing on the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliberate' is the verb, to think over, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder or weigh up carefully is to think something over.

clue.text: Amphitheatre in Trier, in Germany

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A Roman amphitheatre stands in the German city of Trier.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena or circular space for spectacle, as a circus ring or bullring.

clue.text: Sordid Greek partner, according to a Cockney?

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: hubby is a husband, a partner

explanation.surface: A Londoner describes a Greek's husband as seedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class East Londoners, traditionally drop initial H sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty, shabby or seedy; the figurative sense of soiled.

clue.text: Ointment from research centre spilled over motorway

indicators.note: knocked over, so in a down answer the word is turned upside down

parts.note: a lab is a research laboratory
M is the British motorway prefix, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Ointment from a laboratory spills onto the motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A soothing salve or healing cream applied to skin.

clue.text: Hit rower

definitions.meaning: the oarsman nearest the stern who sets the pace for the crew

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a blow or shot, and the rower setting the crew's pace.

clue.text: No thanks! Great! Don't mention it!

parts.note: taken as written
ta is informal British for thanks
great means big, tall

explanation.surface: A string of exclamations: a refusal, delight, and a polite reply.
explanation.definitionFit: A polite reply to being thanked, equivalent to you're welcome.
